proves.claim: the relay lists name reserveItem as an ordered operation whose first argument is an item number.

outbox.relay.reserve-item-names-its-item.why: A reservation whose item number the relay cannot find would be replayed against the wrong item after a renumber.

proves.claim: legacy numeric outboxes remain readable and an old reader refuses new result bindings.

outbox.relay.legacy-readable.why: Old outboxes must stay readable and old readers must not misread new bindings.

proves.claim: a move the relay took is recovered from the ordered log, never posted again.

outbox.replies.lost-reply-recovered.why: A lost reply must not repost a move.

proves.claim: every operation whose reply is lost is recovered once, so submit, verify, edit and merge replies are not re-sent.

outbox.replies.every-lost-reply-once.why: Every operation kind needs the same recovery.

proves.claim: the lost reply of a refused claim surfaces the relay's original rule after the winner, once.

outbox.replies.refused-claim-surfaces-ru.why: The refused side must see the real rule.

proves.claim: three replicas fed one relay order apply the same prefix and agree on every receipt.

outbox.replies.replicas-agree.why: Replicas must converge from one order.

proves.claim: a recovered descriptor with no durable receipt stays pending and is never taken as an outcome.

outbox.replies.no-receipt-stays-pending.why: A guess must not become an outcome.

proves.claim: a receipt for a different sealed record is not this move's reply, so a refusal of the same id is not recovered.

outbox.replies.other-record-receipt-igno.why: Receipts bind to their sealed record.

proves.claim: undo replaces changed values without losing composite bigint and blob keys.

outbox.undo.replaces-changed-values.why: Keys of every type must survive undo.

proves.claim: undo refuses a missing row and rolls back earlier inverses and trigger changes.

outbox.undo.missing-row-rolls-back.why: A failed undo must leave nothing half done.

proves.claim: undo never replaces an occupied row when restoring a deleted row.

outbox.undo.occupied-row-kept.why: Undo must not overwrite newer data.

proves.claim: undo refuses a uniqueness constraint without retaining partial changes.

outbox.undo.uniqueness-no-partial.why: Constraint failures must not leave partial changes.

proves.claim: undo restores a whole changeset with cross-table foreign keys.
undo refuses a foreign key conflict and restores its transaction.

outbox.undo.foreign-key-conflict.why: A conflict must roll the transaction back.

proves.claim: undo rejects an unterminated table header and rolls back its setup.

outbox.undo.unterminated-header.why: Malformed input must not leave setup behind.

proves.claim: unrelated asynchronous callers cannot enter the same outbox guard together.

outbox.guard.unrelated-callers-serialise.why: Concurrent writers would corrupt the outbox.

proves.claim: a guard permits genuine nested work, independent files and reuse after a thrown operation.

outbox.guard.nested-and-reuse.why: The guard must not deadlock honest callers.

proves.claim: a detached descendant cannot reuse an expired guard context while another caller owns it.

outbox.guard.expired-context-refused.why: An expired context must not bypass the guard.

proves.claim: a guard held by another connection is awaited without freezing this process event loop.

outbox.guard.held-guard-awaited.why: Waiting must not freeze the process.

proves.claim: with moves.live.outbox on, a queue and a park leave the outbox in the state the outbox table decides.

outbox.live-record.table-decides-state.why: The live table must decide moves.

proves.claim: with moves.live.outbox on, a move the table refuses is refused with the table's code and next step and changes nothing.

outbox.live-record.table-refusal.why: Refusals must come from the table.

proves.claim: with moves.live.outbox off (the default) the writer's own rules decide and the table is never run.

outbox.live-record.off-writer-decides.why: Off by default means unchanged behaviour.

proves.claim: with moves.shadow off (the default) the outbox writer runs no table and records no compare.

outbox.shadow-record.off-runs-nothing.why: Shadow mode costs nothing when off.

proves.claim: with moves.shadow on, a matching queue and park add one compare each and no disagreement to the outbox table's counts.

outbox.shadow-record.match-counts-compar.why: Matches must be counted, not flagged.

proves.claim: with moves.shadow on, an outbox move whose table answer differs adds one disagreement naming the move and the field.

outbox.shadow-record.differs-counts-disa.why: Disagreements must name the move and field.

proves.claim: every outbox-cell test registered here has a stable ID and one complete record, and an unregistered test is reported and fails only with tests.registryStrict on.

outbox.registry.complete.why: Without a record per test a test can be deleted or duplicated with no one noticing what it proved.

proves.claim: every outbox test file that reads source files carries an input header naming the cells it reads.

outbox.inputs.declared.why: A test that reads files without a header is invisible to affected-test selection and can ship a break unseen.

proves.claim: with relay.queueOnFailure on and a readable key, flushOutbox seals every entry of the unsealed outbox in file order and removes the file only after the sealed write.

outbox.relay-unsealed.folds-in-file-orde.why: Moves kept while the key was unreadable must replay like any queued move and never be lost or sealed twice.

proves.claim: with the key still unreadable, flushOutbox leaves the unsealed outbox untouched.

outbox.relay-unsealed.unreadable-key-lea.why: Without the key nothing can be sealed, so the waiting moves must survive for a later flush.
